_note: All three tools need per-artifact discovery AND per-artifact attribution, which this schema cannot express, so each is driven through the bundled linuxscan.py — one lane entry per tool, so each keeps its own probe, its own clean-skip reason and its own line in the sentinel. rc 3 from the wrapper means 'nothing of this tool's shape under the target' and maps to that tool's skip reason; rc 1 means the run failed.

tools.name: systemd-analyze
tools._note: rc 3 covers both 'no .service under target' and 'not a systemd host'; the wrapper distinguishes them on stderr. The runner's older `requires-systemd-host` reason stays in the vocabulary for the host case.

tools.name: lintian
tools._note: Applicability is a BUILT package (.deb/.udeb/.ddeb/.dsc/.changes//.buildinfo), not `debian/control`. lintian cannot open a source directory at all, so the old `no-debian-source` gate admitted exactly the targets it cannot analyse and excluded the ones it can. Renamed to `no-debian-package` to say what is actually required.

tools.name: checksec
tools._note: One `checksec dir` pass over the target rather than a per-ELF loop, so no ELF discovery is needed. The wrapper accepts both the Go checksec array-with-`checks` shape and checksec-py's path-keyed object.
